content.text: {"approach": "Use the separable incremental-ratio convergence method (Rayleigh/Weibull-style) on the more mature Release A to infer a stable reporting completion curve, then apply that curve to immature Releases B and C to project their eventual totals and estimate unreported defects. Combine reported and projected unreported defects for each cohort, then sum for the organization total.", "steps": ["Analyze Release A cumulative severe defects by week: 40 (w1), 60 (w2), 66 (w3). Compute increments: 40, 20, 6.", "Compute increment ratios for A: w2/w1 = 20/40 = 0.50; w3/w2 = 6/20 = 0.30. These show a clear decay trend, suggesting an asymptotic total.", "Model A as a Rayleigh/Weibull-type growth. Using the increments (40, 20, 6), fit a decreasing geometric progression: ratio step1→2 = 0.50, step2→3 = 0.30. Continued ratio decay is uncertain; assume the ratio halves or follows the observed decline. A conservative geometric model with average ratio sqrt(0.5*0.3) ≈ 0.387 yields projected weekly increments after w3: 6*0.387 ≈ 2.32 (w4), 0.90 (w5), 0.35 (w6), 0.14 (w7), 0.05 (w8), then <0.02. Cumulative A over infinite weeks ≈ 66 + 2.32 + 0.90 + 0.35 + 0.14 + 0.05 + 0.02 + ... ≈ 69.8.", "Alternatively fit A with a sigmoid/S-curve that asymptotes. Assume 90% reporting achieved by week 3 for A (since increments are nearly exhausted at 66 vs ~70 asymptotic). Under 90% completion by w3, A's eventual total = 66 / 0.90 = 73.3. Use this as the asymptotic check.", "Set the final asymptotic total for A at a central value ≈ 71 (between 69.8 and 73.3). Thus A's unreported defects = 71 - 66 = 5.", "For Release B, reported totals are 30 (w1) and 45 (w2). Increment ratio = 15/30 = 0.50, closely matching A's first ratio. Use the same completion curve form as A. At week 2, B has reported 45. If B follows A's ratio pattern (next increment = 45*0.30 = 13.5 at w3), then project increments: 13.5, 4.05, 1.22, 0.37, 0.11... Cumulative B = 45 + 13.5 + 4.05 + 1.22 + 0.37 + 0.11 + ... ≈ 64.3.", "As a check, apply the 90%-by-week-2 view for B. If B's week-2 reporting reflects ~90% of its eventual total, eventual = 45 / 0.90 = 50. But B's ratio pattern (0.50) suggests more remains; use the geometric sum from step 6: eventual ≈ 64. Adjust to a central robust estimate ≈ 62 (capturing uncertainty). B's unreported = 62 - 45 = 17.", "For Release C, only week 1 reported: 20. Apply the same first-increment ratio from A/B (week-1 to week-2 ratio ≈ 0.50). That implies week-2 increment ≈ 20*0.50 = 10, so week-2 cumulative ≈ 30. Then apply subsequent ratios from A (0.30, then decaying 0.387): increments 10, 3.0, 1.16, 0.45, 0.17... Cumulative C = 20 + 10 + 3.0 + 1.16 + 0.45 + 0.17 + ... ≈ 34.8. Central estimate ≈ 35. C's unreported = 35 - 20 = 15.", "Sum projected eventual totals: A ≈ 71 + B ≈ 62 + C ≈ 35 = 168 total severe defects across all releases.", "Compute combined unreported (delayed reporting): (71-66) + (62-45) + (35-20) = 5 + 17 + 15 = 37. Alternatively combined unreported = 168 - (66+45+20) = 168 - 131 = 37.", "Present final estimate: Release A eventual ≈ 71, B ≈ 62, C ≈ 35, combined eventual ≈ 168, combined unreported ≈ 37."], "critical_invariants": ["Cumulative defect totals are non-decreasing; no revision downward of reported counts.", "The reporting-delay curve is stable across releases (A, B, C share the same shape of incremental-ratio decay).", "Eventual totals are finite; late increments eventually fall below 0.5 and are truncated without materially changing the sum.", "Any projected value must be checked against Release A's convergent pattern; do not use the assumed advisory as authoritative.", "Reported values remain exact; only the unreported portion is estimated.", "Combined unreported must equal (sum of eventual totals) minus (sum of currently reported)."], "assumptions": ["Release A's reported pattern is representative of the reporting-delay behavior for B and C.", "Defect reports follow a smooth decaying incremental process with no large spikes in later weeks.", "The time horizon is effectively infinite, but late-week contributions beyond week 8 are negligible (<0.5 defects).", "No independent advisory case was authoritative; the method is grounded purely in the observed A/B/C series.", "The eventual-total estimates are central values, not confidence intervals; actual values may vary by roughly ±15%.", "All releases are in their early phase (A at week 3, B at week 2, C at week 1), so the reported counts do not equal eventual totals."]}
